A technical evaluation framework for testing whether consequential autonomous-agent execution remains continuously bound to an accountable human or institutional mandate through runtime authorization, execution, external state change, independent verification and outcome receipt.

Status: Concept + Evaluation Framework. This note defines an evaluation framework and reports no benchmark results.

What remains unproven:

  • The framework has not yet been validated across a broad public corpus of production agent systems.
  • Metric thresholds are not industry standards.
  • Cryptographic receipts do not prove external truth unless the verification source is trustworthy.
  • Legal authority remains jurisdiction- and institution-specific.
  • Technical enforcement can encode authority but cannot create lawful authority.
  • The public benchmark still needs reproducible fixtures, baseline systems, failure injection and raw result evidence.

Related implementation by the same publisher. The verification-and-receipt principle this note evaluates for agent actions is the one Rūpestėlis Holding applies to its own published content under Article 50 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689): every AI-assisted item Margelis.ai publishes carries a signed receipt that a third party can re-check without an account. Practitioner guidance with primary sources: How to mark AI-generated content under Article 50 and prove the marking is yours; Article 50 readiness checklist (16 checks); EU AI Act in Lithuania: who supervises it and what companies must do. Signed publication registry: https://margelis.ai/verify/. These pages are operational summaries, not legal advice, and are not part of the licensed research note.

Margelis Research Note 001, version 1.1, published by Rūpestėlis Holding. Canonical page: https://rupestelisholding.com/research/001/. Source and release: https://github.com/M12-pixel1/margelis-research/releases/tag/research-note-001-v1.1.
